name: B10-0150/2024 – Motion for a resolution (as a whole)
title: MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/1826 authorising the placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified maize DP23211 pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 1829/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council
part_text:
The European Parliament is asking the European Commission to cancel its decision allowing a type of genetically modified maize, called DP23211, to be sold in the EU for food and feed. The maize is engineered to survive spraying with glufosinate, a weedkiller banned in the EU. Parliament says the approval was not properly assessed, was not supported by a majority of member states, and goes against EU environmental promises. This is Parliament's opinion; it does not itself change the law.

- **What changes:** Nothing yet. Parliament asks the Commission to withdraw the maize approval.
- **Who it affects:** Farmers, food and feed importers, and shoppers in the EU.
- **What happens next:** The Commission must respond; it can keep or cancel the approval.
